producer_report.summary: Root cause: the reader brief listed the reading checks but never the rules that judge a criterion, so readings wrote criteria that contradict them (D43 evidence, in-place edits of docs/decisions.md, forbidding the default-written CHANGELOG.md). The brief now has a `# Rules that judge criteria` section, written by `criteria_judging_section` in reader.rs after `# Checkable criteria`. It has a line each for D43, D63 and D115, an append-only line, and a Changelog line. The D115 line says a passing Athena check on the same tree counts. The append-only line says to use a new appended decision with a Provenance bullet, and a decision-links.toml link only when the entry supersedes or amends an earlier one or touches a [[governs]] path. The Changelog line says a criterion must not forbid CHANGELOG.md. The section is built from pub consts in athena-context. `CHANGELOG_PATH` is now defined once there, and athena-core's reading.rs imports it. Three tests in briefs.rs cover the section, a pin against the enforcing sources (VERDICT_RULES, DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES, and the mirrors, admission and gate phrases), and the drift helpers. No refusal rule or prompt-file edit was added, so the expected share of newly refused readings is 0%. I added CHANGELOG.md and D174 entries. fmt, clippy, the full cargo test, and the policy, mirrors and budgets tests pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-context`. A new test builds the reader brief and asserts it contains a 'Rules that judge criteria' section that states D43's evidence rule (including that a recorded passing Athena check on the same tree counts), that docs/decisions.md and records/ entries are append-only (new decision, not an in-place edit), and that the default-required CHANGELOG.md deliverable cannot be forbidden. The test fails on the base commit and passes with the change.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-context` passed (140 tests). `the_reader_brief_states_the_rules_that_judge_criteria` in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs builds `reader_brief(&reader_inputs(&reading()))` and asserts the heading, and the D43, D63 and D115 lines (D115: a passing check Athena recorded on the same final tree counts). It also asserts the append-only line (both phrases, new appended decision with a Provenance bullet, no 'always add a link'), and the Changelog line (default-written, must not forbid). On the base commit the section and heading do not exist, so the section lookup (`expect`) panics. The base was not rerun.

criteria_check.criterion: A second new test in crates/athena-context shows the section's rule text matches the constants or wording used by the enforcing code, so it fails if the enforcing rule changes and the brief does not. It covers the cause class, not one job.
criteria_check.evidence: `the_criteria_rules_quote_the_wording_the_enforcing_code_uses` reads verify.rs, reading/checks.rs, mirrors.rs, admission.rs and athena-gate lib.rs with include_str!. It parses every id/source pair of VERDICT_RULES and every literal of DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES, and checks each against the section and against VERDICT_RULE_LINES. It checks the append-only and changelog phrases in the production text before the first #[cfg(test)]. `the_drift_helpers_report_a_new_or_reworded_enforcing_row` feeds synthetic extra and reworded rows and shows they are reported. Both pass under `cargo test -p athena-context`.

open_issues: I did not measure whether the added section stops readings from writing contradictory criteria. D174's Provenance says so; the failure class stays in the introspection sweep.
I did not run the replay of past readings. No reading rule changed, so no readings are newly refused.
I did not run the new tests on the base commit; the claim that the first fails there rests on the section not existing.
learnings: The Bash hook for this role denies grep, tail, head, redirection and command substitution; a plain `cargo` command with --quiet gives a compact full-suite summary.
VERDICT_RULES in verify.rs has three rows (D43, D63, D115), not two; the pin test parses all of them.
athena-gate/src/lib.rs has three #[cfg(test)] markers, but the first is after the 'records are append-only' production text (line 101 against 387).
